On the other side, the euro has drawn support from a narrower short-term rate differential with the US, alongside firmer regional PMI readings, elevated oil prices and the prospect of a further ECB hike, a combination that leaves EURUSD positioned to extend gains if the Fed stays on the sidelines. --- Earlier: Gold rises to the highest since May 15 as dollar doom spreads Westpac says dollar's structural headwinds outweigh recent resilience, see EUR/USD and GBP/USD higher --- HSBC says falling US real yields and a narrowing rate gap with Europe are chipping away at its mildly bullish dollar call, with more weakness likely if the Fed stays on hold in September.

title: China leans hardest against yuan gains in six months, AUD softens
body: The scale of this deviation stands out because it comes against a backdrop of broad dollar softness, with the index still hovering near three-month lows on fiscal and debt sustainability concerns. Under normal conditions a weak dollar would be expected to pull USD/CNY lower more freely, so the unusually wide gap suggests the PBOC is working harder than usual to offset that external pull rather than reacting to any fresh domestic weakness. This fits a pattern seen repeatedly since February, where similarly large deviations have consistently been read by analysts as an attempt to slow the pace of appreciation rather than reverse its direction, given the yuan's broader multi-year highs and the currency's roughly 4% year-to-date gain. The Australian dollar, which trades as a liquid proxy for Chinese growth and commodity demand given Australia's trade exposure to China, weakened on the setting, consistent with the pattern of AUD softening whenever the PBOC signals resistance to yuan strength. Other China-sensitive and commodity-linked currencies, such as the New Zealand dollar and South African rand, would typically see similar if smaller pressure from this kind of signal. The near-term implication is a cap on how quickly USD/CNY can fall even as the dollar itself stays weak, with limited signal for the medium-term yuan trajectory beyond that pacing effect.

title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7219 – Reuters estimate
body: The People's Bank of China is due to set the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT (2115 US Eastern time), a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the renminbi (yuan) is allowed to trade within a prescribed band around a central reference rate, or midpoint, set each trading day by the PBOC. The current trading band permits the currency to move plus or minus 2% from the official midpoint during onshore trading hours. Each morning, the PBOC determines the midpoint based on a range of inputs. These include the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies, particularly the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic economic considerations such as capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The midpoint is not a purely mechanical calculation, allowing policymakers discretion to guide market expectations. Once the midpoint is announced, onshore USD/CNY is free to trade within the allowable band. If market pressures push the yuan toward either edge of that range, the central bank may step in to smooth volatility. Intervention can take the form of direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance through state-owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often interpreted as a policy signal rather than just a technical reference point.

Rising oil prices add a complicating cross current, since firmer energy costs could keep inflation elevated and narrow the scope for rate cuts even as fiscal worries support bullion. With July PCE data and Warsh's Jackson Hole speech both on the calendar this week, gold's next move is likely to hinge on whether either event reinforces or eases the debt and currency concerns currently underpinning demand. --- Gold is holding near a three-month high as investors decide that Washington's attempt to manage its borrowing costs is itself the reason to own more of it.

title: Oil is still quietly crossing Hormuz, TotalEnergies CEO says
body: Pouyanne's comments offer a rare on-the-ground account of how physical crude flows are actually adapting to the Hormuz risk premium, suggesting the market has found a working, if quiet, mechanism for moving oil out of the Gulf even as headline benchmarks price in disruption. The scale of the producer discount, as much as $30 a barrel below Brent, points to real desperation among sellers rather than a temporary dislocation, which could keep a lid on how far Brent itself can run even amid ongoing sanctions and shipping risk. The much steeper economics for refined products, where transport costs are effectively prohibitive, helps explain the unusual split Pouyanne describes between a bearish crude market and a bullish products market, a dynamic that could keep crack spreads elevated for as long as the strait remains constrained. Total's continued investment in alternative pipeline routes signals large producers still expect Hormuz risk to be a multi-year rather than transient feature of the market. --- Total's CEO says the strait everyone assumed was closed for business is quietly still open, just at a steep discount only the desperate are willing to accept.

body: The TAIEX, Taiwan's benchmark stock index, dropped 479 points, or 1.0%, to 44,325 in Tuesday morning trading, extending the previous session's losses as weakness in electronic technology and technology services weighed on the market. The index fell to its lowest level since August 7, with both electronic technology and technology services sectors down 1.1%, mirroring the overnight decline in US tech stocks on Wall Street. TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker and a heavyweight that represents more than 40% of the market's total value, slipped 1.4% after a 1.5% decline on Monday. Other major names also retreated, including MediaTek (-0.7%), Delta Electronics (-0.9%), and Hon Hai Precision Industry (-0.8%). Nanya Technology, a key Taiwanese memory chip producer, tumbled 5.1%. Investor sentiment was further pressured by caution ahead of the release of US PCE price data, which will offer clues on the Federal Reserve's policy stance at its upcoming meeting, as well as by upcoming FOMC remarks at the Jackson Hole Symposium. title: Hong Kong Stocks Edge Lower
body: The Hang Seng Index slipped 0.2%, or 39 points, to around 25,475 on Tuesday, mirroring overnight weakness on Wall Street as technology stocks came under pressure. Losses were limited, however, as continued strength in Hong Kong's IPO market helped offset broader risk-off sentiment. title: RBA Flags Inflation Risks Despite Policy Hold: August Meeting Minutes
body: Australia's inflation has eased from its March peak, with underlying price pressures now slightly lower than in late 2025, according to the Reserve Bank's August meeting minutes. Even so, the board judged that inflation remains "too high," with excess demand still evident in the economy. At the same time, financial conditions were viewed as somewhat restrictive, reflecting the impact of previous rate increases. RBA staff forecast that inflation will only gradually return to target by late 2027, and assessed the balance of risks as tilted to the upside. Those arguing for a 25-basis-point rate increase pointed to several such risks: the potential for Middle East tensions to push oil prices higher, firms passing on costs more fully to consumers, stronger investment in AI and data centres, resilient domestic demand, and persistently weak productivity growth. The case for keeping rates on hold rested on accumulating evidence that monetary policy is already restrictive, recent inflation outcomes running slightly below earlier forecasts, and a rise in unemployment. Downside risks to the outlook included a sharper-than-expected easing in labour market conditions, weaker overall demand, and a more pronounced drag from the housing sector. In the end, policymakers left interest rates unchanged but reiterated that they stand ready to tighten policy further if upside inflation risks materialise. title: South Korean Shares Extend Decline
body: The benchmark KOSPI dropped nearly 2% to around 6,570 on Tuesday, extending its losses for a second consecutive session as a global selloff in technology stocks weighed heavily on Korean chipmakers. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix declined more than 3% and 6%, respectively, amid renewed concerns over the profitability of AI-related investments and ahead of Nvidia's earnings release scheduled for Wednesday. Sentiment was further dampened by Samsung's underwhelming shareholder-return plan, which pressured the broader market after the stock slumped 8.7% on Monday. Investors had been anticipating a larger payout and more concrete commitments on share buybacks and cancellations. Meanwhile, attention shifted to the Bank of Korea's policy meeting on Thursday. title: US 10Y Yield Steadies as Traders Weigh Buybacks
body: The yield on the 10-year US Treasury note held near 4.7% on Tuesday as investors weighed the implications of the Treasury Department's expanded debt buyback program. Reports indicated that the US government may draw on its cash balance to fund the additional buybacks, a notable shift given that such operations are usually designed to be cash-neutral and financed through new issuance. On Monday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent declined to offer further guidance on a potential overhaul of US debt management but reassured markets that bond auction sizes would not be cut. Even so, market participants increasingly questioned whether the buyback plan would provide only short-lived relief, reviving worries about the risk of a US debt crisis and potential dollar weakness. Looking ahead, investors were focused on the upcoming release of the US PCE price index and a speech by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh at the annual Jackson Hole symposium later this week, seeking fresh signals on the future path of monetary policy. title: European Natural Gas Holds Gain
body: European natural gas prices remained above €68/MWh, their highest level since January 2023, as new US sanctions on Iran heightened concerns about further disruptions to energy supplies from the Persian Gulf. The US Treasury announced an expansion of secondary sanctions targeting Iran's digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping sectors. It also imposed additional sanctions on 60 entities, individuals, and vessels alleged to be involved in generating oil revenues for Iran, procuring weapons, and supporting cyber operations. These measures have compounded already elevated supply risks in Europe. The ongoing blockade of the Strait of Hormuz continues to restrict LNG shipments from Qatar, a key supplier. This disruption has coincided with stronger cooling demand driven by persistent heatwaves, complicating efforts to rebuild European gas inventories and intensifying concerns that the region may enter the winter heating season with inadequate supply. title: Dollar Steadies as US Tightens Iran Sanctions
body: The dollar index stabilized around 99 on Tuesday, holding its gains from the previous session as safe-haven demand firmed after Washington moved to further cut Iran off from the global financial system. The measures underscored the US currency's central role in international trade and finance. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday outlined plans to tighten Iran's isolation through sanctions aimed at countries that continue to do business with the Islamic Republic. Even so, the dollar hovered near three-month lows after the Treasury Department said it would expand its buyback program for long-dated US government debt in an effort to rein in rising borrowing costs. Market participants questioned how long such measures could remain effective, viewing the plan as potentially only a short-term fix and reviving concerns about the risk of a US debt crisis and longer-run dollar weakness. Investors now turn their attention to the upcoming US PCE price index release and a speech by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh at the Jackson Hole economic symposium later this week, seeking fresh signals on the Federal Reserve's policy path. title: Gasoline Holds Decline
body: US gasoline futures hovered near $3.27 per gallon, extending the prior session's decline as traders assessed the impact of heightened US economic pressure on Iran. title: Gold Extends Rally on Debasement Trade
body: Gold rose above $4,650 an ounce on Tuesday, its highest level in more than three months, as fresh US government intervention in the bond market reignited the so‑called "debasement trade" that underpinned the metal's 65% rally in 2025. Last week, the US Treasury Department announced an expansion of its buyback program for long-dated government debt in an effort to curb rising borrowing costs. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent indicated he is prepared to further increase those buybacks and signaled that a longer-term fiscal plan is forthcoming. Still, markets largely interpreted the steps as a potentially short-lived fix, reviving concerns about the risk of a US debt crisis, entrenched inflation, and sustained dollar weakness. At the same time, gold-backed exchange-traded funds have seen stronger inflows in recent weeks, pointing to broader market participation and reinforcing investment demand for the metal.
